newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Timor protests in support of bishop enter day five.
newsitem.headline: Timor protests in support of bishop enter day five.

text.p: East Timorese protested in the capital of Dili on Saturday in support of Bishop Carlos Belo, hours before the Nobel laureate was expected to return from Jakarta, police and residents said.
Residents said protesters were travelling in convoys of privately owned trucks, cars and motorbikes, a fifth day of such protests which have involved up to 5,000 people.

"There are no problems. The people want to meet the bishop at the airport, but now they are going around the town," East Timor Deputy Police chief Colonel Atok Rismanto told Reuters by telephone from Dili.

East Timorese have publicly rallied around Belo, a popular figure in the territory for his strong stand on human rights, after protests in Jakarta and attacks by Indonesian government officials in the media.
Rismanto said about 500 people were involved in the protests on Saturday morning.
Church sources confirmed that Belo had left Jakarta on Saturday morning after attending an Indonesian bishop's conference as an observer.

In Jakarta, youth groups aligned with the ruling Golkar party, demonstrated against comments Belo reportedly made to the German magazine Der Spiegel that Indonesian troops had treated Timorese like "slaves" and "scabby dogs".
Belo has refused to comment on the article saying he was waiting a full transcript and recording of the interview.

Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in December 1975 and declared the territory its 27th province eight months later in an act never recognised by the United Nations, which regards Lisbon as its administering power.
